operators.customDisplayName: Reload pleasure_bay_and_castle_island_beach_datasheet.csv using pd.read_csv(header=None, dtype=str) to avoid incorrect header inference given multi-row header/section labels; enables downstream parsing by explicitly handling header rows.

Parse pleasureBayData (raw header=None CSV) into a properly headered table by locating the header row (prefers row where first cell equals 'Sample Date'); assign columns while forcing uniqueness (append .1, .2, ...) to avoid duplicate-label indexing errors; select key fields (sample date, site/location, rainfall 1-day prior, Enterococcus count) via fuzzy column-name matching; coerce date to datetime; coerce rainfall/Enterococcus to numeric (strip '<'/'>' qualifiers and non-numeric chars); filter to rows where site contains 'Pleasure Bay' (if site column exists) and to swimming-standard failures where Enterococcus > 104; output standardized columns [sampleDate, site, rain1DayPrior, enterococcus].

Compute the mean rainfall in the 1-day period prior to sampling (rain1DayPrior) among Pleasure Bay Beach samples that failed swimming standards (Enterococcus > 104), then round to 2 decimal places; also report counts of failed rows and non-null rainfall values.
